title: Antimicrobial Characterization of Advanced Materials for Bioengineering Applications
protocol: Cut the material samples into 10 mm diameter disks using a 10 mm diameter cylindrical punch.
Soften brittle materials in suitable sterile solvents for 1 h before cutting if necessary.
Moisten hydrophilic materials like zinc alginate in autoclaved water before cutting to prevent sample breaking.
Dry the sample material disks at 60 °C in a vacuum oven (<10-2 Torr) for 24 h.
Measure the thickness of each material film using a digital caliper.
Sterilize each specimen by immersing it in ethanol 70% for 10 min.
Expose sterilized specimens to UV radiation for 1 h per side inside a sterile Petri dish under a 12.0 W lamp of UV-C radiation in a laminar flow hood.
Prepare and autoclave tryptic soy agar (TSA) following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Pour TSA into sterile Petri dishes under aseptic conditions using a Bunsen burner or a laminar flow hood.
Culture different microorganisms aerobically for 18–24 h in Petri dishes with TSA in an incubator at 37 °C.
Prepare and autoclave tryptic soy broth (TSB) following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Pour TSB in a 50 mL pre-sterilized centrifuge tube using a sterile serological pipette under aseptic conditions using a Bunsen burner or a laminar flow hood.
Resuspend a few colonies from step 3.1.3 in 25 mL of TSB contained in a sterile centrifuge tube using a sterile cotton swab.
Vortex the culture for 1 min to achieve a uniform mixing.
Adjust the absorbance (at 540 nm) of the culture with a spectrophotometer to approximately 1.5 x 10^8 CFU/mL for bacteria and from 1 x 10^6 to 5 x 10^6 CFU/mL for yeast.
Vortex the microbial broth for 5 seconds to improve microorganism dispersion.
Briefly submerge a sterile cotton swab in the microbial suspension.
Remove excess liquid from the swab by pressing it against the tube wall containing the culture.
Evenly streak the microbial broth suspension with the sterile cotton swab onto the surface of the TSA plates in 3 planes to cover their whole surface.
Let the inoculated TSA plates dry for 5 minutes.
Place the TSA plates open in an inverted position at 37 °C for 10–15 min before inoculation to remove any moisture.
Sterilize a pair of tweezers by immersing them in ethanol 96% and flaming them with a Bunsen burner or alcohol burner.
Place the sample disks to be tested and control disk at the center of the TSA plates using the sterile tweezers.
Incubate aerobically the TSA plates in an inverted position at 37 °C for 24 h.
Dispense sterile TSB into sterile microcentrifuge tubes using a micropipette with suitable autoclaved tips in aseptic conditions.
Utilize one tube as a negative TSB control.
Perform decimal serial dilutions of the microbial broth suspension in sterile microcentrifuge tubes containing TSB.
Spread 100 µL of each dilution on TSA plates using a pre-sterilized Drigalski spatula or an alternative instrument.
Spread 100 μL of TSB medium without microorganism on a TSA plate as a negative control.
Incubate the TSA plates aerobically at 37 °C for 24 h.
Count the number of colonies to check that the CFU/mL are similar to those determined previously.
Check for microbial environmental contamination on the TSA plates with only one type of colonies.
Ensure there is no microbial contamination on the TSB negative control plate showing no colonies.
Dilute the overnight culture in 20 mL of TSB in a 50 mL pre-sterilized centrifuge tube to achieve approximately 10^6 CFU/mL.
Perform decimal serial dilutions of this culture in sterile microcentrifuge tubes containing TSB.
Spread 100 µL of the culture on TSA plates and incubate it aerobically at 37 °C for 24 h.
Count the number of colonies to ensure an initial cell concentration of approximately 1 x 10^6 CFU/mL.
Place 4 control disks for microbial counting after 24 h and 4 sample disks of each type of tested material in separate wells of a sterile 48-well plate.
Pipette 150 µL of the microbial suspension onto each disk surface.
Aerobically incubate the 4 sample disks remaining in the 48-well plate at 37 °C for 24 h.
After 24 h of incubation, pipette 850 µL of sterile PBS onto the surface of the 4 sample disks.
Mix the PBS with the microbial suspension on each disk.
Collect the PBS/microbial suspension mixture and each disk from the 48-well plate.
Transfer the collected samples to a 10 mL pre-sterilized tube.
Vortex the PBS/microbial suspension mixture for 1 min.
Sonicate the mixture at 50 Hz for 5 min.
Vortex the mixture again for 1 min.
Perform decimal serial dilutions of each sonicated culture in sterile microcentrifuge tubes containing TSB.
Spread 100 µL of the culture on TSA plates.
Incubate the plates aerobically at 37 °C for 24 h.
Count the number of colonies to determine the number of viable microorganisms.
Express the number of viable cells in CFU/mL.
Take a photograph of the final microbial culture for the sample and control disks.
Measure the diameter of the inhibition zone and the disk diameter with a digital caliper.
Determine the normalized width of the antimicrobial halo using equation (1).
Calculate the mean and standard deviation of the normalized width of the antimicrobial halo from the four determined nwhalo values of each sample.
Take a photograph of the final microbial culture with the material disk.
Measure the diameter of the inhibition zone and the disk diameter from the photograph taken if necessary, by using image processing software.
Determine the number of viable microorganisms recovered according to equation (2).
Determine the loss of viability to reflect the inhibition of cell growth using equation (3).
Calculate the average number of viable microorganisms in CFU/mL•cm² from control specimens after 24 h.
Measure the number of viable microorganisms in CFU/mL•cm² from test specimens after 24 h.
Determine the mean and standard deviation of the loss of viability with the 4 determined LV(%) values of each sample.
